scope: Frozen 1828–1836 incoming corpus as possible prompts or knowledge sources for January–March 1837 outgoing letters.
methodology: Read the complete retained bodies and editorial notes for the five plausible late frozen incoming witnesses (Fox 197/261, Henslow 249, Whitley 267, Caroline 300), then the complete January–March 1837 outgoing bodies. Checked participant direction, explicit references, dates and whether a source could actually supply the stated prompt or knowledge. No relation was inferred from date proximity alone.

outgoing_boundary_records.assessment: No frozen incoming prompt; the letter is a farewell following a face-to-face evening.

evidence.quote: As I have not seen you to wish you good bye in propriâ personâ, I must do it, on paper.

outgoing_boundary_records.assessment: No frozen incoming prompt; this is a same-day social cancellation with no cited earlier letter.

evidence.quote: I was so unwell all yesterday with a bad cough, that I am very so[rry] I shall not be able to dine with you to day

outgoing_boundary_records.assessment: No frozen incoming body from Whewell was located. The explicit proposal is acknowledged, but its source is absent from the frozen incoming set.

evidence.quote: I have taken the whole day to consider the proposal, which you have made me in so kind a manner.

outgoing_boundary_records.assessment: Fox 261 and 197 were read as the closest surviving Fox letters, but neither is a safe prompt: 197 is January 1833 and 261 November 1834, while 348 says only “your last letter” and supplies no matching distinctive content. A later missing Fox input remains possible.

evidence.quote: In your last letter you urge me, to get ready the book.
It is now so long since I have heard from you
I had hoped to have heard a few lines from you in the last 5 months

outgoing_boundary_records.assessment: No frozen incoming prompt; Darwin declines Babbage’s invitation for the next evening and gives no letter reference.

evidence.quote: I am very much obliged for your kind invitation for tomorrow evening

outgoing_boundary_records.assessment: No frozen incoming prompt; this is Darwin’s editorial recommendation on Williams’s paper, based on the paper’s contents rather than a surviving incoming letter.

evidence.quote: I should, therefore on the above grounds, suggest that Mr Williams’ paper

outgoing_boundary_records.assessment: No frozen Henslow letter is a demonstrated prompt. Henslow 249 was read in full but concerns 1834 shipment and field-work correspondence, not this 1837 publication plan; 353 itself says the plans were unsettled when Darwin last saw Henslow, indicating oral context or an unlocated input.

evidence.quote: I do no think when I last saw you, that our plans about publication were settled.
I have not your letter bye me to answer your questions formally

candidate_relations.reason: Fox 261 is the only read Fox source that discusses Darwin’s return and future correspondence, but its 1834 date and lack of the book-publication wording make it inadequate as a direct prompt. A later missing Fox letter is more plausible.

evidence.quote: I hope you will experience as much delight in the South Sea as you anticipate
In your last letter you urge me, to get ready the book.

candidate_relations.reason: Both concern Henslow–Darwin scientific work, but 249 is from 1834 and contains no identifiable 1837 publication prompt; retain only as remote background, not a reply edge.

evidence.quote: I recommended the fossils to be all sent to Mr Clift
Now the scheme that the Captain makes a plum pudding out of his own journal

rejected_relations.reason: Caroline 300 is a March 1836 family letter about Darwin’s imminent return and family news, not the January 1837 farewell’s immediate source; 339 explicitly refers to the previous evening in person.

evidence.quote: I can hardly believe how near home you will be

rejected_relations.reason: Whitley’s 1835 mathematical-professor discussion does not contain Whewell’s 1837 Geological Society proposal and has the wrong correspondent.

evidence.quote: I think you were aware of my being a candidate for the office of Mathematical Professor
the proposal, which you have made me

missing_evidence_limits: The frozen corpus ends before January 1837 and does not contain a surviving Whewell, Babbage, or late Fox/Henslow prompt matching the new outgoing letters.
Old letters can establish background knowledge only when their content, participant direction and chronology support it; they cannot replace an unlocated immediate input.
No canonical annotations, maps or raw data were changed.

quote_validation.method: Manually checked every quoted substring against the retained packet bodies before writing.
